topic_coverage.quoted_user_text: Operators who want its-magic's artifact workflow without Cursor's soft rules, BYOK-subagent ceiling, and alias-only models. They need real subagents, own provider keys including Chinese APIs, and host-enforced behavior.

Authoring in this git repo. Operator runtime is stock OpenCode TUI/desktop/IDE, not a vendored OpenCode binary. Consumer repos get .opencode/ via the its-magic installer. Headless uses US-0092 --invoke-cmd.
Kernel stays Python 3 validators and existing scripts. Adapter plugin is OpenCode plugin TypeScript/JavaScript. Agents and thin commands are markdown plus JSON under .opencode/.

Host-adapter on unmodified OpenCode: kernel artifacts plus validators plus auto_outer_driver plus US-0069 matrix; host pack is .opencode/agents, thin commands, and one orchestrator plugin. Cursor pack remains. Rejected: OpenCode fork, greenfield runtime in this repo, VS Code plus shell rewrite.
No new its-magic GUI in v1. Operators use OpenCode TUI/desktop/IDE. Kit UX stays slash-command names and ASCII CLI diagnostics with reason codes.

Never read .env in plugin logs. Provider keys stay in OpenCode /connect auth store, not git, not template vendor slugs. Plugin must not print API keys. Role permission deny-lists are the security control. Kit does not proxy traffic.
Priority 1 enforceability of spawn permissions and validators. Priority 2 Cursor coexistence. Priority 3 fail-closed reason codes. Priority 4 template parity. Priority 5 TUI polish is out of kit v1.

v1 is OpenCode adapter in this repo: install pack, seven roles with permissions, thin commands, orchestrator plugin, per-role models, docs and tests. Out of scope: standalone runtime, OpenCode fork, VS Code contrib rewrite, Caveman, Cursor browser UAT, full sovereign-loop parity.
